card.name: Just before a dosing or monitoring interval
card.fires_on: Punctuation or small words right before a repeating schedule is named, such as every 2 weeks, monthly, or annually. It fires in dosing and lab-monitoring schedules, where the next word is likely a frequency.

modes.label: Bracket before Q-code
modes.description: An opening parenthesis after an every-N-weeks dose that is followed by an abbreviation like Q2W or Q4W.

modes.label: Lead-in to monitoring frequency
modes.description: A comma, colon, or 'least' that introduces how often to check labs, with monthly or every N weeks expected next.
modes.example: monitor hemoglobin levels at least weekly until stable, then monitor at<< least>> monthly.

card.writes: It pushes the model toward interval words such as monthly, bi-, and quarterly, and away from vague words like regularly or frequently.
card.plain: It marks the spot where the text is about to say how often something is given or checked, such as monthly or every few weeks.
